provenance: Manufacturer list and summaries verified against bolexcollector.com page titles and indexed page content (search-index recovery, 2026-07-26). Individual lens listings per manufacturer/decade are populated by the preservation pipeline from archived pages.

manufacturers.name: Kern-Paillard
manufacturers.summary: Kern lenses of Aarau, Switzerland were the premier optics supplied for Bolex cameras across the 1940s, 1950s and 1960s, including the RX series computed for the reflex prism of the H-16 Reflex cameras.

manufacturers.name: Hugo Meyer
manufacturers.summary: Pre-war Bolex cameras were often equipped with Hugo Meyer lenses, a German manufacturer of photographic lenses founded in the late 1800s.

manufacturers.name: C.P. Goerz
manufacturers.summary: Founded in 1886 by Carl Paul Goerz in Berlin. The Goerz Kino-Hypar was an air-spaced, three-element motion picture lens used by both professional and amateur cinematographers.

manufacturers.name: Wollensak
manufacturers.summary: Established in 1899 in Rochester, NY. Good quality construction priced much lower than Kern lenses; a popular choice with amateurs throughout the 1940s and 1950s.

manufacturers.name: SOM Berthiot
manufacturers.summary: Société d'Optique et de Mécanique Berthiot produced C- and D-mount motion picture lenses for professional and amateur use, as well as the Pan Cinor series of zoom lenses.

manufacturers.name: Angénieux
manufacturers.summary: Documented on the original lens index alongside Kern-Paillard, Hugo Meyer, Goerz, Wollensak and SOM Berthiot; dedicated pages pending recovery.
